newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Portugal and Spain sign telecoms deal.
newsitem.headline: Portugal and Spain sign telecoms deal.

text.p: Portugal Telecom and Spain's Telefonica on Wednesday signed a cooperation deal aimed at exploiting their joint strength in Latin America.
The two companies sealed the accord with a small exchange of shares, with Telefonica taking a 3.5 percent holding in its Iberian neighbour and Portugal Telecom reciprocating with a one percent stake.
"Both Portugal Telecom and Telefonica believe this agreement will reinforce their strategic objectives, linking and strengthening the interests of both companies," Telecom said.

The accord came hard on the heels of an announcement earlier this week that Portugal Telecom had opted to join the Anglo-American international alliance Concert, a move which also has at its heart development of Latin America's burgeoning market.

The Portuguese decision to hitch up with British Telecom and MCI has stoked speculation that Telefonica could be about to abandon its alliance with rival international grouping, Unisource, which is led by.
The accord between the two Iberian telecommunications companies would involve cooperation in future privatisations expected in Brazil, where both already have interests, and in North Africa.
Portugal Telecom planned to take a small stake in CRT, a Brazilian fixed line operator in which a consortium including Telefonica recently bought a 35 percent share.
Portugal Telecom would also be invited to take part in Telefonica's plans for a new venture to build and operate a Latin American intercity network, the statement said.
It was also expected that there would be interchanges of technology and expertise in areas such as research and development, network operations and human resources.
